blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: V-Shaped Valleys are formed as a direct result of vertical erosion.
Gorges and Canyons represent deep river valleys characterized by steep sides.
Waterfalls occur at points with a sudden drop in the river's course.
Rapids consist of turbulent water flow moving over an uneven bed.
Potholes are circular depressions created on river beds specifically by abrasion.

blocks.content: • Gorges and Canyons – deep valleys with steep sides.
• Waterfalls – sudden drop in river course.

items: Competitive exams frequently test the specific process of 'vertical erosion' as the cause of V-Shaped Valleys.
Distinguish between Potholes (formed by abrasion) and Rapids (turbulent flow over uneven beds).

blocks.content: • Rapids – turbulent flow over uneven bed.
• Potholes – circular depressions formed by abrasion.
